title: Alerting rule templates and user flows brainstorm
content:
Purpose:
Quick brainstorm and rough wireframe notes for a lightweight template-driven alerting UX. Goal is to let product and SRE teams create common alert rule patterns quickly, map them to channels and escalation policies, and preview user-facing flows without needing to write YAML or open infra tickets.

Context and why: 
- Observability/alerts in Console are fragmented: people create ad-hoc alerts per model/route; no shared templates, so on-call fatigue + noisy channels.
- We want: lower friction for non-SREs to onboard alerts, consistent thresholds by SLO class, and readable playbooks for responders.

Key assumptions: 
- Most customers will rely on a few canonical templates (Latency, Error-rate, Throughput drop, Token-cost spike, Model-quality regression).
- Templates should expose a small set of editable knobs: metric selector, threshold type, window, severity, channel set, runbook link.
- Templates must map to SLO tiers (gold/silver/bronze) and recommend escalation.

Draft UX components (list view -> template editor -> preview -> publish):
1) Template gallery (cards)
   - Filter by category: SLO, Runtime, Billing, Model Quality
   - Each card shows example condition, default severity, recommended channels (Slack/email/pager)
   - Quick actions: Duplicate, Customize, Assign to team

2) Quick-create modal using a template
   - Step 1: Select template (Latency / Error / Drift / Cost)
   - Step 2: Scope: Global | Model | Route | Dedicated pool (autocomplete resource picker)
   - Step 3: Thresholds: simple slider or advanced expression editor (toggle)
   - Step 4: Channels & Escalation: pick from saved channel bundles or quick-add (Slack workspace -> channel, Email list, PagerDuty service, Webhook)
   - Step 5: Preview & test: simulate an alert using synthetic inputs; show eventual message payload + suggested runbook snippet

3) Template editor (for power users)
   - YAML-like behind the scenes but GUI-first. Visible fields: name, description, metric query, operator, threshold, window, severity, SLO impact estimation (approx tokens/requests at risk), recommended remediation steps, runbook link, tags
   - Recommended defaults per SLO tier: e.g., Gold latency: p95>300ms for 5m -> severity P1; Silver: p95>500ms for 10m -> P2

4) Escalation & policy composer
   - Visual timeline: On trigger -> wait X minutes -> notify channel set A -> if not acknowledged in Y -> escalate to B -> page on-call
   - Support for holdouts: maintenance windows, quiet hours per channel, team overrides

5) Playbook preview panel
   - Human-readable incident playbook auto-generated from rule + runbook snippets (one-click copy to incident response tool)

Concrete template examples to seed gallery (samples for tests / product):
- Latency - p95 increase: metric=route.latency.p95, operator=>, threshold=300ms, window=5m, severity=P1, recommend channels=[pagerduty:oncall, slack:#infra-alerts], SLO-tier=gold
- Error rate - 5xx spike: metric=route.errors.5xx.rate, operator=>, threshold=1.5%, window=10m, severity=P1, channels=[slack:#errors, email:owner], auto-snooze during deploy flag
- Token-cost anomaly: metric=cost.per-1000-tokens, operator=>, threshold=+40% vs baseline, window=60m, severity=P2, channels=[billing-email, slack:#costs], action=auto-scale down suggestion via Runbook
- Model-quality regression: metric=evaluation.f1.rolling, operator=<, threshold=-3% vs baseline, window=24h, severity=P2, channels=[ml-team, pm], runbook=rollout-rollback-template

Unresolved questions / tradeoffs (notes to self):
- How opinionated should default channels be? Risk: over-notification vs under-notify. Proposal: template recommends but owner decides.
- Should we allow per-template rate-limits (suppress X alerts per Y)? Useful to cut noise but complicates semantics with SLO detection.
- Integration surface: PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Slack, Email, Webhooks only for MVP. Do we need MS Teams? (ask GTM: EMEA customers prefer Teams)
- Multi-tenant considerations for Dedicated: channel mapping needs enterprise-safe scoping and admin approvals.

Edge UX flows and corner cases:
- Template changes mid-flight: show a list of derived alerts and prompt to re-evaluate their thresholds. Must ask for explicit re-deploy for safety.
- If a template is deleted, what happens to active rules? Provide orphaned rules report + auto-migrate tool.
- Partial failure of channel delivery: show retry state and fallback to escalation channel B automatically.

Wireframe sketches (ASCII / notes):
- Gallery -> left pane categories, center grid of cards, right panel live-preview. Clicking card expands editor in modal overlay.
- Quick-create: 3 column modal: left = scope picker, middle = settings, right = preview/test panel (message example + expected recipients)

Metrics to validate success:
- Time-to-create-alert (target < 3 mins from template selection to publish for quick-create)
- Reduction in unique alert rules per workspace (target -30% in 90 days)
- Mean number of channels per alert (monitor to detect over-notification)
- On-call acks > 90% within recommended window for P1 alerts (operational metric)

Implementation notes for eng:
- Backend: store templates as JSON schema + version history. On change create diffs for derived rules.
- Rule engine: support templated metric queries with parameter substitution (resource, percentile, baseline window)
- UI: prototype with React playground + storybook components. Keep advanced editor collapsible.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- [ ] Prototype gallery and quick-create flow (Priya + Jared) - 2 sprints
- [ ] Draft sample templates for the 5 canonical cases and validate with SREs (Maya)
- [ ] Add Teams integration ask to GTM backlog (Liam)
- [ ] Run a small usability session with 3 customers to validate quick-create (PM-led)

Notes to reviewer: 
This is intentionally light on visuals; want feedback on the template knobs we expose and which channels to recommend by default. Also want input on threshold presets by SLO tier — I included a few ideas but need SRE sign-off.

Slack refs and tickets:
- convo: #console-alerting (thread pinned: "templates-ideas")
- draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console-prototypes/pull/128
- internal design spike: RD-4821

Random notes / brain dump (keep for traceability):
- Consider a checkbox "auto-create incident on trigger" for teams that prefer immediate incident lifecycle.
- Allow template sharing across organizations (with admin opt-in) — good for professional services + partners to ship best-practice sets.
- Export templates as JSON for infra-as-code users to import into Terraform later.

End of doc.
